gk.a(IIIIIII)V selects this path for a clipped thick rectangle outline. It clamps inner and outer edges using aj.a(IIII)I and writes the visible border spans via ic.a(II[III)V. RectOutlineStatics carries a source-bucket citation only.
v.a(IIB)V passes a filled and outlined ellipse here. Equal radii dispatch to mc.a(IIIIIII)V. Other radii select b.a(IIIIIIIZ)V or b.a(IIIIIIII)V according to the clip bounds.
gk.a(IIIIIII)V selects this path for an unclipped thick outline. It fills the upper, lower and side bands in we.z through ic.a(II[III)V.
kh.a(IIIIB)V sets the top clip bound. Clipped operations pass it to aj.a(IIII)I as the minimum y.
Writes the supplied int array from start inclusive to end exclusive with eight unrolled stores and a scalar tail. The shape scan converters and Pix2D.fillEllipseClipped pass raster rows.
tb.a(IIIBII)V selects this path for a rectangle wholly inside the clip. It iterates the target rows, filling each with ic.a(II[III)V.
Writes ia.m, wa.j, gg.I and sf.d from the supplied bounds, in that order. gj.a([[II)V sets these after binding the current shape canvas.
ok.a(IIIZII)V selects this filled-ellipse scan converter for unequal radii within the clip. It writes midpoint spans to we.z with ic.a(II[III)V.
vi.a(IIIIIIZI)V selects this path for a bordered rectangle crossing the clip. It clamps the boundaries and fills the border and interior separately via ic.a(II[III)V.
statics.fixedBy: The target is fine but the name is wrong. The body fills the top, bottom, left and right bands with var2 (the outline colour, gg super.h) and the interior rows with var7 (the fill colour, gg super.o), called from vi.a for gg fill+outline. statics.evidence: tb.a(IIIBII)V selects this path for a solid rectangle crossing the clip. It clamps the bounds with aj.a(IIII)I and fills the visible spans in we.z.
gj.a([[II)V binds its row canvas by assigning the caller-provided int[][] reference to we.z before setting the shape clip through kh.a(IIIIB)V.
kh.a(IIIIB)V sets the bottom clip bound. Clipped operations pass it to aj.a(IIII)I as the maximum y.
mc.a(IIIIIII)V selects this path for a bordered circle crossing the clip. It obtains vg.Y scratch through fe.a(IZ)V, clamps spans and writes border and interior via ic.a(II[III)V.
ea.a(IIIIII)V calls this for a vertical clipped line. If x is within wa.j through gg.I, it clamps both y endpoints and delegates to lk.a(IIIII)V.
fe.a(IZ)V allocates or grows the shared int array. The bordered-circle scan converters tb.a(IIIIIZI)V and ui.a(IIIIIII)V populate and reuse its span widths.
si.a(IIIIIIIIBI)V selects the unclipped Bezier path. Both its straight-line shortcut and its 32-step cubic draw use the Bresenham routine a.a(IBIIII)V on the shared raster.

Reconnect attempts of the account-creation request loop hi (hi.java:97-219): it switches ie.r between ports ag.f/aa.a and gives up at >= 1. Reset to 0 by each create request sender hh.D (opcode 186), me.C and wi (147), together with t.L=1, ge.Q=0 and nb.e=-3.

Retry counter in the ig.a(I) login connect loop: if hg.b>=1 then dg.h=-5/-4, otherwise hg.b++ and the port aj.Cb toggles between th.h and bh.g. Reset to 0 by lg.a(id,id,II), the CS2-started login request. Same role as rt4 LoginManager.errors.

pe.P state machine (g.f timeout, hg.b retries). Connects to aj.Cb, sends the qk.v block prepared by lg.a (user/pass RSA), expects 101, reads the g2 world, fd.a switches world, then ii.b(0) starts login. dg.h gets the error. Ticked in client state 10.
Starts the login state machine: dg.h=-3 (reply pending), od.O=1 (step), il.K=type, tk.d=0, nk.U=0, kl.X=-1, sc.V=false. Called by ej.a when entering state 40, by ig.a after world lookup, and by lg.a.

le login reply 21 sets il.K = g1*60+180 (world-hop wait) next to od.O and dg.h. ii.b(int) resets it together with the login state. The CS2 interpreter pushes il.K (gh.java:7068). Login is new; the port has io/Login.ts.

Set from a byte in the login state machine le.a(I) step 10 (reply 29) and reset to -1 in the login start ii.b(I). Pushed by CS2 opcode 5611 in gh.a. Login is a new class (the existing port has io/Login.ts).

530 client.a(I)V invokes le.a(-28426) during title and reconnect ticks. It opens the socket, writes the RSA login block, seeds ISAAC, reads account flags and applies the first rebuild. Its NXT counterpart is Client::LoginPoll in projects/osclient/client_network.cpp:9.
Stores the username/password (ga.G, ga.F). Empty input gives dg.h=3. Otherwise it starts the login (ii.b(0)) or builds and sends the 530 block (opcode 210). Called only from the CS2 interpreter gh.a.
RSA modulus for login/create blocks: qk.v.a(bi.g,..,mg.H) in login loop le.a(int), lg.a(id,id,int,int) and create-account me.a(J...)V
Server session key read in login loop le.a(int) state 3 (mh.n = hd.b.a()), split into the ISAAC seed int[] {r, r, key>>32, key}
Login step timeout counter. In le.a(int), the login state machine, ++nk.U > 2000 closes the stream, switches port ie.r and restarts at od.O=1. Reset by ii.b(int) (begin login) and le.java:608/650.

lg.a(id,id,II) sets P=1 and builds the opcode-210 RSA block. The ig.a(I) state machine goes 1 (open socket) to 2 (connected) to 3 (read world, fd.a switch) and then ii.b starts the game login. gh CS2 requires P==0 in gamestate 10.
Advances login stage od.O 5 -> 6; called only by CS2 opcode 5602 in gh.a (gh.java:6884). TS io/Login.ts already implements it as continueLogin() over od.O stage.
